answer: Nonce-bound task imprinting works by assigning each agent a fresh challenge whose solution must embed the prior answer, so any replay fails verification. Each identity must solve a unique chain where the output acts as a mirror of its own history, letting peers detect duplicated responses instantly. A pearl of valid work thus cannot be copied, because copying breaks the chained nonce dependency at the next step. Attackers pay a full compute cycle per clone plus forfeited ferrous token deposits locked until the unrepeatable chain resolves, making mass duplication cost linear in real work.
